(PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI)

Petitioners who are arraigned as accused Nos.2 and 3 have filed this petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. with a prayer to quash the entire proceedings in C.C.No.5817/2022 (private complaint No.4/2022) for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 109, 504, 506, r/w Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 27 and 39 of the Indian Arms Act, 1959 pending on the file of the I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Hubballi.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:18084 2.
In support of the petition, the petitioners have contended that the private complaint, consequent FIR and charge sheet filed against them are not tenable.

The marriage of respondent No.2 and accused No.6 was performed on 20.05.2001 and after 20 years of marriage, she has chosen to file a false complaint implicating the petitioners also who are her mother-in-law and father-in- law.
There are no specific allegations against the petitioners.

Already, the charge sheet against accused Nos.1 Neelakanth S/O Fakkirappa ... vs The State Of Karnataka on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88494224/
2 and 6 came to be quashed on the basis of the settlement between them and respondent No.2 in Crl.P.No.100695/2023.

entities.text: Neelakanth S/O Fakkirappa ... vs The State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The charge sheet against accused No.5 is quashed in Crl.P.No.102896/2022.

In the absence of specific allegations against the petitioners and in the light of the quashment of criminal proceedings against accused Nos.1, 5 and 6, no purpose world serve by continuing the prosecution against the present petitioners and pray to allow the petition.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:18084 3. Learned HCGP respondent No.1-State and learned counsel for respondent NO.2 complainant submitted oral objections.
4.
Heard arguments and perused the records.

5. Respondent No.2/complainant filed a complaint under Section 200 of Cr.P.C. against accused Nos.1 to 6 including the petitioners alleging offences punishable under Section 354, 509, 420 r/w 34 of IPC.
It was referred to the concerned police for investigation.

After conducting detailed investigation, the concerned police have filed charge sheet against accused Nos.1 to 3, 5 and 6.
6.
Accused No.5 got the criminal proceedings against her quashed in Crl.P.No.102896/2022.
Accused Nos.1 and 6 got the criminal proceedings against them quashed in Crl.P.No.100695/2023 by way of compromise.
The petitioners are the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the complainant.
The main allegations are against the husband of respondent No.2 who is accused No.1.

Though NC:
2024:KHC-D:18084 certain allegations are also made against petitioners, in the light of settlement between accused Nos.1 and 6 and also quashing of the criminal proceedings against accused No.5,
no purpose would serve by proceeding with the trial against the petitioners.
After due service of notice, respondent No.2 has appeared through counsel.

The entire proceedings initiated against the petitioners/accused Nos.2 and 3 in C.C.No.5817/2022 (private complaint No.4/2022) for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 354, 109, 504,
506, r/w NC: 2024:KHC-D:18084 Section 34 of IPC and under Sections 27 and 39 of the Indian Arms Act, 1959 pending on the file of the I Additional Civil Judge and JMFC, Hubballi, are hereby quashed.

Sd/-
